channel.title: NPR Topics: Education
channel.description: We've been to school. We know how education works. Right? In fact, many aspects of learning — in homes, at schools, at work and elsewhere — are evolving rapidly, along with our understanding of learning. Join us as we explore how learning happens.

item.title: The Education Dept. hasn't been dismantled. It's become more inefficient, staff say
item.description: Education staff are being scattered across several other federal agencies. Despite the Trump administration's claims, employees say it's adding bureaucracy and making it harder to serve students.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: How the NPR College Podcast Challenge changed lives
item.description: Five years later, the first-ever winner of the NPR College Podcast Challenge looks back at her early work in journalism and talks to other participants about where their stories have taken them.

item.title: The Senate is about to pass a bill that promises to bring stability to college sports
item.description: A bipartisan bill making its way through the Senate would reshape the rules of the road around college sports, but critics say it benefits schools while limiting the benefits to student athletes.

item.title: NPR's College Podcast Challenge is back for 2026
item.description: Students: It's time to turn on the mic and hit 'record.' Send us your podcasts and we'll pick the best ones. It's $5,000 for our grand prize and $500 for our finalists.

item.title: DEI and colleges
item.description: The President of Sacramento State talks about their Black honors college -- and how schools are dealing with DEI under the Trump administration. This story was produced with support from the Education Writers Association's Reporting Fellowship program.

item.title: Head Start got her out of homelessness. Trump proposal threatens that help for others
item.description: A Trump administration proposal would change access to Head Start for children experiencing homelessness and the kind of care they would receive if they do get in.

item.title: When students attend these colleges, taxpayers often pay. Here's why
item.description: Federal data shows many borrowers who aren't paying their loans went to private, for-profit colleges — schools that often market to low-income students and rely on federal financial aid for revenue.

item.title: The colleges where borrowers aren't repaying their student loans
item.description: Millions of federal student loan borrowers are in default or well on their way. New federal data shows that tens of thousands of them attended the same problematic schools.

item.title: In Florida, textbook publishers are minimizing or removing climate change coverage
item.description: The words "climate change" are slowly being removed from textbooks in Florida and from the state's education standards.
